Well this isn't really a confession but I needed somewhere to say this anonymously so I'll just say it here. It's a bit of a rant and most of you probably don't care so you can probably just close this thread if you wan't, I won't mind.

I've spent most of my adult life totally isolated from any emotional contact with other people. I was beaten down too many times as a child, and eventually I just gave up and stopped caring about others. I became very good at faking interest in things, really faking every emotion because on the inside I felt next to nothing. I ended each day having gained and lost nothing because I emotionally 'wagered' nothing at all. I lived like this for many years, and I was more or less content to stay that way.

Many years ago, near the beginning of when I started to live like this, I met a girl. She had the same first name as my middle name, and was similar to me in a LOT of ways. She, too, didn't reveal much of herself to the world. We talked a lot and I bought her coffee once. After a year or so our paths stopped crossing and we never really talked again. I didn't think much of it, or of her, because I was absolutely convinced that real emotional contact was just a fairy tale.

Fast forward to earlier this year. I met another girl, two actually, who were the same way. Reclusive, hidden, and strikingly similar to myself. But they had each other, and they seemed really close for some reason. I couldn't understand it. I spent a lot of time conversing with these two girls, getting to know their stories. Nothing serious, of course, but we became close enough where I could safely call them friends.

After a few months of this I was convinced. I saw the immensely strong friendship that these two girls had and I went on a month-long journey of self realization that led to me vowing to end my reclusive ways. That is not the focus of this story.

About a week ago one of these girls disappeared. The other one won't tell me what happened to her (only that "She'll be gone for awhile..." in a sad-sounding voice) and I have honestly no idea what happened. I have a really nasty feeling that something bad happened to her and I honestly don't know if I can take the loss...it's been so, so long since I've had a real bond with someone, I can't imagine what I'd do if suddenly one of those bonds were broken. The other girl is moving away next year...I don't want to be alone again, but at this rate I'm not sure if I even want to be awake.

I know this is irrelevant to all of you reading, I just wanted to type this out so I could see the story with my own eyes. I'm seriously shivering typing this, because I'm horrified of both possible outcomes - I'm horrified of returning to my old ways, but I'm also horrified of remaining this vulnerable, where even the THREAT of emotional loss is enough to disturb me thoroughly.

It's subjective. Have you seen the latest version? I think it is by far the prettiest yet.

It's barely POSIX compliant (what retarded ass version of UTF-8 does HFS use?). Thanks to the App Store's DRM it's also limited to GPL2 software instead of GPL3, so congrats on having a ten year old Bash.

Even with all of it's bullshit and issues, Apple really does do a gorgeous interface. It's only when you want to do something that Apple doesn't think you need to do that you run into problems.

1. Cost: It's free but so is BSD. Linux is tied with BSD. Inconclusive.

2. User interface: Very subjective and too many desktop environments to compare. (kde, gnome, unity, pantheon, openbox, xfce, cinnamon, mate... list goes on.) Inconclusive.

3. Security No operating system is or ever will be impervious but open source operating systems are generally considered to be better at resolving vulnerabilities in a timely manner once one is found. Furthermore because the source code is public open source operating systems are supposed to be more resistant to nation states. Inconclusive.

4. Fan-club Lately, I find the linux fan club almost as annoying as the apple fan club. BSD community wins here because the community is the most mature community. They won't scoff at you for using M$, apple or linux.

5. Choice and Customizability Linux wins here hands down. Plethora of DEs and Distros, which ironically is also a con for some people. Inconclusive.

**Conclusion: ** No operating system is the best, use whatever makes your dick hard. I use Arch with gnome 3, would I recommend it to my mother? Hell no. Would I recommend linux or BSD to a friend that games? No, I would recommend Winders because ATM it gets the job done better than linux in that area.
